topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional primary cancer treatment modalities and their respective mechanisms and systemic limitations.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted strategies designed to exploit specific cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the targeting of hyperactivated kinases in oncogene-addicted cancers and the molecular mechanisms underlying therapy resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the engineering and application of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively target cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for tumor immune surveillance and therapeutic strategies that harness or engineer T cells to eliminate cancer.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate clinical challenges, historical outcomes, genomic stratification, and future ethical considerations in managing cancer.
